name: Apache AGE
model: PostgreSQL extension: property graphs queried with openCypher inside SQL (SELECT * FROM cypher(...)), next to normal tables
engine_note: Each vertex and edge label is an ordinary Postgres heap table with B-tree indexes; traversals become joins planned by Postgres
consistency: Inherits PostgreSQL: ACID multi-row transactions mixing graph and relational changes; read committed default, serializable as option; fsync on commit by default; streaming replicas can be stale.
scaling: Same as the Postgres it runs in: bigger machine, read replicas; no graph-aware sharding.
version_note: Released per Postgres major version; GitHub tags carry '-rc0' even for releases. PG18 1.8.0 on downloads.apache.org dated 2026-08-06; PG15 1.8.0 still a candidate.
reach: Reach for it when you already run Postgres and want some Cypher graph queries over data that also lives in normal tables, in one transaction.
avoid: Avoid for deep traversals over very large graphs where native graph stores are much faster, or on managed Postgres that does not offer the extension.
escape: graph queries in Cypher without leaving Postgres or adding a second database
chat: Graph of users, chats and mentioned entities kept inside the same Postgres as the chats.
notes: Azure docs (ms.date 2026-06-08) confirm AGE is available as an extension on Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server and that it uses Postgres's ACID transaction system. The engine_note's 'one table per label' is supported by the ag_label catalog having a 'relation' column pointing to the backing table. GitHub marks PG15/v1.8.0-rc0 (2026-09-19) as prerelease 'pending PMC approval'. age.apache.org front page is stale (still mentions 1.5.0 for PG16). Amazon RDS and Google Cloud SQL support for AGE not checked; not listed. No Jepsen analysis.
